stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The model is associated with Meta's Llama family, indicating relevance in the large language model space.

stories.title: Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: The EU's AI Act transparency rules are now active, specifically targeting AI identification.
Companies must now disclose when users are interacting with AI models (e.g., chatbots).
The regulations also mandate disclosure for AI-generated content, such as deepfakes.

stories.title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: US company is providing advanced AI capabilities to Ukraine's existing drone fleet.
The deal involves equipping 50,000 Ukrainian kamikaze drones with autonomous target tracking.
The total value of the agreement is reported to be $100 million.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 achieves significant speed improvements on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates within the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing LLM execution on Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is running AI functionality entirely on the user's own device.

stories.title: Microsoft is bringing Xbox 360 games to PC
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding its PC gaming strategy to include Xbox 360 titles.
The move allows third-party developers to port their Xbox 360 games to PC.
This initiative builds upon Microsoft's existing plans to bring original Xbox games to PC.

stories.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
stories.author: Zhichao Cao
bullet_points: TokTier addresses an inefficiency in LLM serving where front ends re-tokenize full requests instead of leveraging cached KV state.
The problem is particularly acute for coding agents that frequently append small tool results to long transcripts, complicating token boundary reuse.
Empirical data shows that while most calls append significant text (median 1.4K characters), session rebuilding remains a major overhead.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality is now available within the Claude Code environment via Ollama.

stories.title: Your Fitbit data can now connect directly to Apple Health
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Fitbit data can now integrate directly with Apple Health via a Google Health update.
The feature is accessible through the Fitbit profile icon under 'Partner apps'.
This integration allows users to sync workouts, steps, and vital statistics between platforms.

stories.title: An AI-supervised remote exam went so badly that 58,000 students must retake it
stories.author: Nate Anderson
bullet_points: AI-supervised remote exams experienced significant failure.
The system led to a 5x increase in top scores, indicating potential bias or flaws.
58,000 students were required to retake the flawed examination.

stories.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
stories.author: Simon Suo
bullet_points: Introduces ExtractBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for schema-guided enterprise document extraction.
The benchmark uniquely evaluates multiple critical metrics simultaneously: value accuracy, record completeness, grounding, and measured cost.
Addresses the growing industry need for AI agents to reliably extract structured data from complex enterprise documents based on predefined schemas.

stories.title: AgentHPOBench: A Benchmark For Evaluating LLM Agents as Sequential Hyperparameter Optimizers
stories.author: Xuanjing Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AgentHPOBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLM agents' capability as sequential hyperparameter optimizers.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation, which often focuses on static tasks rather than dynamic, evidence-guided experimentation.
Highlights the growing importance of evaluating LLMs as autonomous scientific agents capable of interpreting experimental results to inform future decisions.

stories.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
stories.author: Dylan J. Foster
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Imitation Learning (IL), specifically the compounding errors of standard Behavior Cloning (BC).
It investigates the role of on-policy interaction in improving IL performance when perfect expert representation is unattainable.
The research explores representational tradeoffs as a means to enhance agent learning from expert demonstrations.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark for testing dyadic familiarity inference.
Evaluates multimodal LLMs (text, audio, video) against human panels on short social interaction clips.
Focuses on the non-verbal cues and interaction manner to determine if two individuals are familiar or strangers.

stories.title: TraceViT: Grounded Trace Supervision for Visual Abstract Reasoning
stories.author: Wei Hua
bullet_points: Introduces TraceViT, a new looped visual reasoner designed for visual abstract reasoning tasks like ARC.
Addresses a limitation in conventional training where intermediate refinement steps in iterative reasoning are unconstrained.
Proposes training the model to follow the transformation step-by-step using grounded trace supervision.

stories.title: DungeonBench: A Benchmark for Rules-Rich Tactical Reasoning in Dungeons & Dragons Combat
stories.author: Kaan Oktay
bullet_points: Introduces DungeonBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for testing rules-rich tactical reasoning.
The benchmark focuses on simulating complex decision-making found in Dungeons & Dragons combat.
It addresses a gap in current AI benchmarks by requiring models to handle interactions involving geometry, timing, resources, and specific game rules.

stories.title: Sign compression for Muon: SignMuon, MuonSign, and the Limits of Error Feedback
stories.author: Alexey Kravatskiy
bullet_points: Introduces SignMuon, a method to compress the Muon update to one bit per parameter using elementwise sign.
SignMuon achieves superior practical performance compared to SignSGD while operating under a very low communication budget.
The research highlights limitations in gradient signing placement, demonstrating that signing before the LMO is crucial for avoiding ascent on simple functions.

stories.title: GQ-FSL: Green Quantized Federated Split Learning
stories.author: Lutz Lampe
bullet_points: Addresses energy and resource constraints when deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) at the wireless edge.
Proposes Green Quantized Federated Split Learning (GQ-FSL) to overcome overheads in traditional Federated Split Learning (FSL).
Aims to reduce energy consumption associated with continuous data and submodel exchange in edge AI deployments.

stories.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
stories.author: Dylan J. Foster
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Imitation Learning (IL), specifically compounding errors in standard Behavior Cloning (BC).
It investigates the role of on-policy interaction in improving IL performance when perfect expert representation is unattainable.
The research explores representational tradeoffs as a method to enhance agent learning from expert demonstrations.

stories.title: A Human-Centered Validation of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient
stories.author: Luis F. Lago-Fernández
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for trustworthy Explainable AI (XAI) in high-risk domains.
Proposes a new model-agnostic metric, the EPC score, to quantify explanation quality.
The metric explicitly balances explanation fidelity with performance, focusing on human-centered understanding.

stories.title: QASP: Query-Adaptive Robust Vector Search Policy
stories.author: Andy Warfield
bullet_points: Addresses the core problem in vector search: balancing high recall with low computational cost.
Introduces QASP, a novel policy that predicts the full recall progression curve for each query.
Moves beyond average recall evaluation to address significant performance variance across individual queries.

stories.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs
stories.author: Adam Sobey
bullet_points: Addresses the interference problem in Multi-Policy LLM training when using shared PEFT methods like LoRA for heterogeneous tasks.
Proposes a novel optimization strategy to move beyond the limitations of relying on a single shared optimization path.
Focuses on improving task sequencing and adapter composition for better transfer learning and mitigating catastrophic forgetting in LLMs.

stories.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Xipeng Qiu
bullet_points: The paper introduces WCM, a World Critic Model designed for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Reinforcement Learning.
It addresses a critical limitation in current RL approaches for robotic manipulation: critics often rely only on single-frame observations.
WCM aims to overcome the exponential complexity associated with naively incorporating full observation history into the critic.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark for assessing dyadic familiarity inference.
Evaluates multimodal LLMs (text, audio, video) against human panels using 20-second conversation clips.
Focuses on the non-verbal aspects of social interaction to determine if individuals are familiar or strangers.

stories.title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
stories.author: Shuo Shang
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for efficient long-context inference by tackling KV cache compression.
Existing compression methods either permanently discard information (eviction) or risk perturbing retained data (merging).
The proposed method, ResKV, formulates omitted attention contributions as residual statistics to enable better reconstruction.

stories.title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation
stories.author: Simon Pietro Romano
bullet_points: Introduces ARB, a new benchmark dataset designed to test AI-text detectors under realistic conditions.
Addresses a gap in current research by evaluating detectors when human-authored text is rewritten by LLMs, not just direct LLM output.
The dataset is built from 1,800 human source texts, aiming to provide a more robust evaluation of text detection capabilities.

stories.title: Evidence-Type Competition: When Can Interventional Data Teach Language Models Causal Direction?
stories.author: Xining Xun
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that interventional data is always sufficient to teach causal reasoning in Language Models (LMs).
In synthetic environments exhibiting Simpson's paradox, increasing interventional data does not improve the model's ability to infer causal direction.
The study demonstrates that the magnitude of the model's 'do()'-response grows monotonically, even when correlation and causation conflict.

stories.title: Know It, Act on It: Investigating Memory Utilization in LLM Personalization
stories.author: Emmanuele Chersoni
bullet_points: Memory utilization is a critical, emerging capability for personalized LLM agents.
A key challenge is the 'knowledge utilization problem,' where LLMs may fail to act on relevant user preferences even when the data is in context.
The research aims to distinguish between a failure to remember information versus a failure to effectively use remembered information.

stories.title: Bridging the Question-Answer Gap in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings
stories.author: Aleksandar Tošić
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems: the style mismatch between user queries and retrieved document text.
It proposes a method involving 'Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings' to improve alignment between the query and the retrieved context.
The research aims to mitigate the computational overhead associated with existing runtime solutions like HyDE while enhancing RAG accuracy.

stories.title: Token Cost Optimization: The Complete Guide to Building Cost-Efficient LLM Applications
stories.author: abhishekjaiswal_4896
bullet_points: Focuses on token cost optimization for LLM applications, a critical operational concern.
Addresses the fundamentals of token economics and hidden costs in AI development.
Targets AI engineers looking to build more cost-efficient LLM solutions.
